title: Catalog baseline-signature + adaptive calibration playbook for per-model quant defaults
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a repeatable, instrumented playbook that produces a per-model "baseline signature" (dataset-aware accuracy sensitivity vector) and an adaptive calibration workflow that recommends FP8/INT8 defaults plus hard guardrails for the model catalog. This ticket captures the engineering design, validation harness, rollout plan, and safety fences for exposing per-model quant defaults to the catalog and runtime. The focus is on minimizing accuracy regressions while unlocking cost improvements via aggressive mixed precision for eligible workloads.
implementation_plan: 1) Implement lightweight baseline signature extractor (Model + representative dataset sampler) that outputs per-layer sensitivity scores and token-length sensitivity distributions. 2) Integrate signature generation into model onboarding pipeline (catalog ingestion hook). 3) Build adaptive calibration runner that executes shadow quantized inference (FP8/INT8/mixed) against a configurable eval set and collects accuracy deltas, confidence drift, and output divergence metrics. 4) Produce a recommended default profile and hard guardrails (max acceptable accuracy delta, fallback chain). 5) Surface recommendations in catalog UI and expose API for runtime to enforce guardrails. 6) Add CI gating and rollout canary for catalog changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Baseline signature successfully generated for 10 canonical models and stored in catalog metadata.
- Calibration runner produces per-model recommendation (profile + confidence band) and a human-readable rationale.
- Automated check flags any recommendation that exceeds the configured accuracy delta (default 0.5% top-line OR application-specific threshold).
- Runtime honors guardrails: if recommended profile would violate SLO in production, fallback to safe variant.
- Documentation (Confluence) and runbook for on-call included.
- End-to-end demo: catalog shows recommended profile, engineer can approve and promote to runtime canary.
decision_log: 2025-08-16: Chose layered sensitivity + dataset fingerprinting as the baseline signature instead of full end-to-end eval because it reduces eval compute by ~3x while preserving signal for per-layer quant risk.
2025-08-22: Opted for two-tier defaults: recommended_profile (soft) and enforcement_guardrail (hard). Soft defaults appear in UI; guardrails are enforced by runtime policies.

2025-08-27: Selected a shadow evaluation harness for calibration (shadow inference with sampled traffic and static eval sets) rather than rolling production A/B for initial rollout to avoid customer exposure.

2025-09-01: Decision to use mixed FP8 where supported, with INT8 fallback for hardware without FP8 support; quant profiles include per-layer exceptions for attention/output layers identified by sensitivity > 0.8.
2025-09-03: Agreed to store original FP32 checksums and a minimal golden set per model for regression auditing and future re-calibration.
progress_updates: 2025-08-18: Prototype extractor implemented; runs end-to-end on small models (L2) against synthetic fingerprints. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1798
2025-08-25: Calibration runner v0 integrated with CI and outputs CSV of layer-sensitivities + accuracy deltas. Internal dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/quant-calibration/overview
2025-08-30: First recommendations generated for five candidate models. Noted consistent degradation in one family when applying FP8 to final layer; added per-layer exception rule.
review_feedback: PM (Julie Chen) 2025-08-26: Request to expose both absolute and relative accuracy deltas for enterprise customers. Action: add delta types to runner output.
Design (Samir Shah) 2025-08-29: Catalog UX should show explainable rationale for each recommended change (bullet reasons + impact estimate). Action: include rationale field in metadata and DTO.
Security (Lina Novak) 2025-09-02: Verify that signature artifacts do not leak customer PII. Action: anonymize dataset fingerprints and store only hash summaries.
risks:
- Overfitting recommendations to small eval sets can cause false positives/negatives in production. Mitigation: require multi-dataset checks and randomized sampling.
- Hardware heterogeneity: FP8 not uniformly available across partners/cloud regions. Mitigation: supply explicit fallback chain and runtime capability check.
- Latency/regression risk if per-layer exceptions are not applied correctly. Mitigation: add preflight dry-run and per-route canary.
- Catalog churn risk (many models with similar defaults) could overwhelm ops. Mitigation: batch rollout windows and thresholds for auto-approve.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for extractor and runner metrics.
- Integration tests that replay representative eval sets against FP32, FP8, INT8 variants and assert delta thresholds.
- Shadow canary on <5% internal traffic for models with approved recommendation.
- Manual review for any recommendation with accuracy delta > 0.2% or customer_impact=high.
- Regression test suite saved as part of model metadata for future calibration.
rollback_plan:
- Immediate runtime fallback to last known-good profile if post-rollout telemetry shows accuracy regressions > configured guardrail within 1 hour.
- Automated rollback ticket generated and notify owners.
- Re-assess with expanded eval sets and adjust per-layer exceptions before re-deploy.
open_questions:
- Thresholds: should catalog default absolute delta be 0.5% or 0.2% for public models? PM leaning towards 0.5% but enterprise customers may require 0.2%.
- How to represent uncertainty/confidence bands in the catalog UI without confusing non-technical users?
- Do we allow auto-approve for low-risk models with consistent calibration results across datasets? If so, define criteria.
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: initial rollout is catalog-only recommendations with a shadow-run approach. Future work (follow-up tickets) will look at auto-promotion heuristics and cost-vs-accuracy optimizer. Coordinate with runtime team for enforcement APIs (ENG-21034 referenced for autoscaler interplay).
